messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — elevated 5xx + latency from us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Auto-created incident. initial metrics: hosted-api 5xx ~15% (1m rolling), dedicated-pool-us-east p95 latency 2.4s, error mix: ELB 503s + STS 429s. Pager: paged @elaine-sre and @jason-oncall.

elaine-sre: ack. I'm on it. First pass: pulling gateway error breakdown (ELB vs application), token errors, and QPS distribution across instances. Adding tags: region=us-east-1, impact=high, service=hosted,dedicated.

kevin-runtime: seeing a clear spike in STS throttles and ELB 5xx backend errors. Sample from edge logs: ```
[2025-08-14T14:10:03Z] proxy=gw-12 us-east-1 backend=svc-gen status=503 "upstream connect error" x-request-id=req-0a1b2c
[2025-08-14T14:10:05Z] auth=sts status=429 "Rate exceeded" user=redwood-service
```
Also health check against a few dedicated backend hosts returns 503: ```
curl -sv https://dedicated-us-east.internal/health
* Connected to dedicated-us-east.internal (10.0.2.15) port 443
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: dedicated-us-east.internal
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< content-type: application/json
{"ok":false, "reason":"upstream-econnrefused"}
```
Kept seeing elevated connect errors to AWS STS endpoints (regional). Could be regional control-plane throttling at the cloud provider level.

ana-platform: thanks, Kevin. I'm going to flip routing policy to reduce weight to us-east-1 and drain non-critical Dedicated pools in that region. Suggestion: 1) divert 70% of new traffic to us-west-2 2) mark us-east-1 pools read-only for model uploads and scale down autoscale triggers 3) enable cross-region fallback for customer requests that previously pinned to us-east-1. I'll post exact commands.

ana-platform: running: ```
# reduce weight to us-east-1
rctl routing set --region us-east-1 --weight 30 --reason "regional AWS degradation"
# increase us-west-2 weight
rctl routing set --region us-west-2 --weight 70 --reason "regional AWS degradation"
# start drain on non-critical dedicated pools in us-east-1
rctl pools drain --region us-east-1 --policy non-critical
```

elaine-sre: doing quick runbook checks — see runbook "regional-cloud-dep-outage" (internal link) for handoffs and customer comm templates. We're going to: triage cause (cloud API vs infra), implement routing mitigation (Ana), and prepare status page + customer notices (Jason/Amy).

jason-oncall: opening status incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-089 (draft). Draft message: "We are seeing elevated errors and latencies for services in AWS us-east-1 due to third-party regional API degradation. Traffic is being routed away from the region and some Dedicated pools are in a degraded state. Engineers are actively mitigating. More updates in 15 minutes." Any edits before I publish? :mega:

amy-cs: pls include a note about customers with region-locked Dedicated pools — some will be impacted even with routing changes. I already have two active support tickets: CUST-4217 (health checks failing) and CUST-4221 (high latency on embeddings). I'll start sending the standard "investigating" template to the affected accounts and attach the draft status page.

kevin-runtime: additional note — model-serving layer is experiencing KV cache misses due to retries against KMS/STS causing request pileups. Short-term mitigation: reduce continuous-batching window for us-east-1 to reduce tail latency and reduce retry attempts for STS calls. Proposed patch: ```
# lower batching window to 5ms for us-east-1
rctl config set --scope region:us-east-1 serving.batch_window_ms 5
# reduce token refresh retries
rctl config set --scope region:us-east-1 auth.sts_max_retries 1
```

ana-platform: applied routing changes. ops-bot shows: "routing weight update accepted (us-west-2:70, us-east-1:30)". Initiating drain on non-critical pools. Note: this will cause short-lived cold starts for some flows.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary change deployed: reduce-batching-window (rev: 2025.08.14-rc3) to us-east-1-slice-1. No rollback detected so far.

elaine-sre: monitoring dashboards — after routing change we see hosted-api 5xx drop from 15% -> ~6% within 2 minutes; dedicated p95 latency improving from 2.4s -> 1.1s for diverted traffic. Remaining errors concentrated on pinned dedicated pools and STS/KMS calls.

jason-oncall: status page published. Customer comms queued for impacted accounts. Escalating to cloud provider support (AWS) for STS/KMS/ELB anomalies; raised ticket 1234567890 — attaching logs.

amy-cs: update: CUST-4217 confirmed reduced errors for multi-region customers. Region-locked customers still seeing failures; sending targeted note and offering short-term credit.

kevin-runtime: still seeing occasional 503s from internal proxy to upstreams in us-east-1. I'm enabling a temporary fallback to a compatible model variant hosted in us-west-2 for latency-sensitive endpoints (embeddings/chat). Patch: ```
rctl feature-flag set --flag cross-region-variant-fallback --enabled true --regions us-west-2
```

ana-platform: cross-region fallback enabled. Also set automatic retry jitter off for region-bound requests to avoid thundering herd.

elaine-sre: quick customer-impact summary for incident ticket: "Root cause under investigation: increased AWS regional control-plane/API errors (STS/KMS/ELB) in us-east-1 causing elevated 5xx and latency for Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Mitigations: traffic diversion to us-west-2, drained non-critical pools in us-east-1, reduced batching window, limited STS retries, enabled cross-region model fallback. Immediate impact: multi-region customers reduced errors; region-locked dedicated customers remain impacted. Next actions: await AWS response, continue draining and monitoring, prepare post-incident RCA."

jason-oncall: handing off to next oncall @kevin-runtime for H+2. I'm on until 14:45 UTC, will monitor for 15 min then drop. Escalation contact list updated in incident ticket.

kevin-runtime: acked. I'll be owning follow-ups. Requesting observability team to snapshot traces for affected windows (14:05-14:25 UTC) and keep retention high for 72h.

ops-bot: observability-bot: snapshot created /traces/snap-20250814-1405-1425, retention set 72h.

elaine-sre: short-term update (14:25): customer-visible 5xx now ~3%, p95 latency stabilized ~600ms for diverted traffic. Closing immediate mitigation loop; keeping incident open for RCA and cloud provider feedback.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (traffic diversion + fallbacks applied). Severity: Sev2 -> Monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for RCA notes and postmortem.
